title: The 'EDF deputy' conflict-of-interest questions
description: After being elected in 2022 following an eight-year career at EDF (2014-2022), Bregeon served as rapporteure on the 'energy' part of the 2022 purchasing-power bill and then, from February 2023, as rapporteure of the nuclear acceleration law. A January 2023 Mediapart investigation by Jade Lindgaard, headlined 'Questions sur Maud Bregeon, la deputee EDF', and critics including environmental groups questioned whether her former employment at the state utility created a conflict of interest on nuclear legislation. Bregeon stated she had resigned from EDF after her election 'to have a free hand' and said she had consulted the National Assembly's ethics ombudsman (deontologue), who concluded she was not in a conflict-of-interest situation, having no remaining contractual or financial links with EDF.
status: No formal finding of conflict of interest; the Assembly's ethics ombudsman concluded there was none. Allegation/criticism only; no legal proceedings reported.
key_facts: Worked at EDF 2014-2022; resigned upon election in 2022.
Rapporteure of the 2023 nuclear acceleration law.
January 2023 Mediapart investigation raised conflict-of-interest questions.
She consulted the Assembly's ethics ombudsman, who found no conflict of interest.
No legal proceedings; presumption of innocence applies to any allegation.
